sections.markdown:
## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: signal lights, arrows, intersections, right-of-way and pedestrians
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from this section's selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge or memory.
The freeway entry and exit figures printed on the first selected page come through the extracted text only as scrambled labels; only the clear exit instruction (slow down in the exit lane, not on the freeway) is taught [A01].
The T-intersection drawing on the second selected page labels one vehicle as having the right-of-way; only the printed rule is taught, not the drawing [A02].
The manual prints the dark-signal rule twice, once for inoperative signals and once for uncontrolled intersections; both are taught from their own pages [A02].
The pedestrian-activated signal list on the last selected page is taught exactly as printed; the manual does not say how long each phase lasts (verify AZ-SIG-D-HAWK) [A03].
Originality: every statement is reworded from the cited page; no manual sentence, table, image or official test question is reproduced.
Exam numbers: the manual prints no question count, passing score, item format or time limit, so none is stated anywhere in this section; the typed debts live in part A.
External review: restating published Arizona traffic and licensing rules needs no clinical or legal sign-off; none is requested.

corpus_stability.reason: The Arizona Driver License Manual carries one revision line on its contents page (Revised September 2026) and points to Arizona Revised Statutes Title 28 for current law; nothing in the selected pages signals more than one rewrite per year.

verification_debt.claim_text: The pedestrian-activated crosswalk signal indications are listed in words without a picture of the signal head in the extracted text; confirm the signal appearance from the rendered page or an official ADOT source before illustrating it.
